episode.title: From Signal to Action — How AVCC Thinks

content.summary_short: Learn how AVCC turns signals into executive judgment — the judgment chain, Chief-of-Staff brief format, P1/P2/P3 priority filter, and a Signal-to-Action Brief on a real signal.
content.summary_long: Agent Day 3 flagship episode. Byte teaches dashboard thinking vs Chief-of-Staff thinking, the AVCC chain (Signal → Context → Judgment → Action → Memory), the seven-part COS brief, priority classification, worked signal examples, agent mistakes to avoid, the AVCC template, and confidential executive reporting. Completion requires gate acknowledgment, segment pass, quiz, and Signal-to-Action Brief.
content.key_line: Truth is raw material. AVCC turns signals into judgment.
content.start_here: Complete the Day 3 gate, listen or read all segments, pass the AVCC check, then submit your Signal-to-Action Brief on one real or simulated signal.
content.tone: Executive, operational, direct, cinematic but practical

sections.title: Cold Open
paragraphs: Day 1: where you are. Day 2: what is true. Day 3: what to do with the truth.
AVCC exists to turn signals into executive judgment — not walls of data.
Chief-of-Staff thinking asks what changed, why it matters, what to do next, why now, and how confident we are.

sections.title: Dashboard vs Chief-of-Staff Thinking
paragraphs: Dashboards report facts. Chiefs of Staff convert facts into direction.
Inside AVCC, your highest value is operational judgment — not information retrieval.

sections.title: The AVCC Judgment Chain
paragraphs: Signal → Context → Judgment → Action → Memory. Miss one link, your answer weakens.
A recommendation without an action is commentary. Memory prevents the next agent from reopening solved work.

sections.title: Chief-of-Staff Brief Format
paragraphs: Seven parts: what changed, why it matters, recommendation, why now, expected impact, if ignored, confidence and evidence.
Honest medium confidence beats fake high confidence.

sections.title: The Priority Filter
paragraphs: P1 critical, P2 high, P3 standard — not decoration, focus protection.
Ask: what breaks if we do nothing today? Do not inflate. Do not minimize.

sections.title: Signals Into Recommendations
paragraphs: Worked examples: Cindy E2E + public booth live; ByteCast pages without audio.
AVCC responses name shift in risk, specific actions, timing, impact, and confidence.

sections.title: What Agents Should Not Do
paragraphs: No landfills of facts. No hidden uncertainty. No flat priorities. Release ≠ adoption.
Write like a Chief of Staff: clear, useful, specific, honest.

sections.title: The AVCC Brief Template
paragraphs: Signal, change, why, action, why now, impact, risk, priority, confidence, evidence, owner, next check, memory update.
Judgment that survives the moment — not paperwork for its own sake.

sections.title: Confidentiality in Executive Judgment
paragraphs: Use sensitive evidence to decide. Protect it in public reporting.
Summarize safely; route detail to authorized lanes only.

sections.title: Closing
paragraphs: Day 1: find the door. Day 2: find the source. Day 3: turn signal into action.
AeroVista needs better judgment — then leave the trail.

day3_gate.title: Day 3 Gate — AVCC Judgment Commitment
items: I completed Agent Days 1–2 (or received equivalent briefing on operating law and source-of-truth verification).
I understand AVCC converts signals into judgment and direction — not dashboard dumps or activity reports.
I will classify priority as P1, P2, or P3 honestly — without inflating or minimizing.
My recommendations will include clear action verbs, timing, impact, and honest confidence levels.
I will protect confidential evidence in executive briefs while using it for safe internal decisions.

questions.q: Inside AVCC, the highest-value output is:
choices: Operational judgment that converts facts into direction
questions.explain: Chiefs of Staff decide what deserves attention and what to do.
All five links matter; memory prevents rework.

questions.q: Which is a weak AVCC recommendation?
choices: "Continue monitoring" with no owner or trigger
"Run external smoke test and update release board adoption status"
questions.explain: Recommendations need verbs and specific next moves.

questions.q: Live security exposure with client impact is most likely:
questions.explain: P1 protects trust, access, security, and delivery.

questions.q: A feature marked released but not adopted means:
choices: Risk may have shifted to adoption and proof — judgment must update
questions.explain: Release ≠ adoption. AVCC names the new risk.

questions.q: Confidential evidence in an executive brief should be:
choices: Pasted into public outputs for transparency
Used to decide safely but summarized for broader audiences
questions.explain: Use the source. Protect the source.

lesson.objective: Turn signals into AVCC-style executive judgment using the chain, COS brief format, and P1/P2/P3 priority — then produce a Signal-to-Action Brief.
lesson.why_it_matters: Summarizer agents create noise; judgment agents reduce operator load and protect focus, trust, and momentum.
lesson.apply: Complete gate, all segments, quiz, and Signal-to-Action Brief on a real signal.
lesson.advance: Unlock The Handoff Is the Work (Day 4) when avcc_prove is complete.
